system.summary: Syllabic code of numbers 1 to about 550, one number per letter, syllable, common word or name, with homophones; written as dash- or point-separated numbers inside clear French. Probably the 'chiffre' that reached Baudouin from de Neufville by 30 March 1779; who composed it is not shown.

prior_solution.where: No edition of this correspondence or its code was found. PBF 28:354 n.9 cites the 23 Feb 1779 Baudouin note (p.495) with recipient unknown; the volume's 19th-century index names 'Du Noyer, Bowdoin or Mad. D. Arras'; Butler's 1978 index lists 'Van Temmel'.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.

solution.what: Found the free NARA Catalog copy of the file (file unit 464816476, 808 images) and mapped Fold3 page numbers to its frames.
Transcribed de Neufville's enciphered fair draft pp.604-606 twice and aligned it with his plain draft on p.599 (19 April 1779, 'Mad. d'Arras').

Built key K1 (139 numbers) only from his interlined drafts pp.600-603 and 609, froze it, and predicted pp.604-605: 139 of 146 covered groups as in his draft; 200 shuffled keys at most 15. Held-out pairs: 8 of 10, shuffled at most 3.
Key K2 (170 numbers) frozen with the whole 6 May 1779 draft (p.608) held out: 64 of 65 covered groups predicted; 200 shuffled keys at most 7.
Added the recipient's glosses over Baudouin's letters pp.516-548 and 579; full key 204 numbers frozen (key_full_r3.json).

Checked on the leaves the volume's 19th-century index identification 'Du Noyer, Bowdoin or Mad. D. Arras': letters of 23 Feb and 7 Mar 1779 signed 'Baudouin', the second saying he will in future sign a name from the enclosed little cipher (and that he is making a cipher); same hand later signs 'Dunoyer'.
Read the bare groups of pp.491-492 and 573 with the frozen key; two unglossed lines of p.527 decoded but not read.

Searched Founders Online, HathiTrust full text (incl. search-only Schulte Nordholt and van Winter), Cryptiana and the repository: PBF 28:354 n.9 cites the 23 Feb 1779 Baudouin note (recipient unknown); nothing prints the letters' text, content or code.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 305 tokens, 119 types, fr-1750-nospace order 4: reading -2.099 per letter; random keys -3.504 (z 9.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.188 (mean -2.219, z 4.1); annealer on the real text -2.077. Verdict: pass.

A second AI agent of ours took 183 pairs from drafts pp.599 and 601 before seeing the key (87 of 94 numbers agree), confirmed 38 of 39 further entries on the images and reran the three tests identically. Its corrections (224 m/n, 381 is 384, 9 deux/da, 71 on/mme) are checked on the images and kept in key/corrections_post_test.tsv; the frozen keys are unchanged; no reading changes.

Integration check of PR #587. The three tests rerun from the pair files: T1 139 of 146 (shuffles max 15 of 200), T2 8 of 10 (max 3), T3 64 of 65 (max 7); the three key hashes equal key/FREEZE.txt. Own T1 with 2,000 shuffles: mean 1.8, max 23; 139 is 77.7% of all 179 groups with a draft unit (33 are not covered by K1). An independent decoder built from the pair files gives the same 204-number key and the same decodes of B573, B491, B492 and B527; one difference: 136 has one vote each for 'a' (accented) and 'au', the frozen key holds the first, the decode file prints 'au'. Images fetched from the National Archives Catalog (frames 0428, 0363, 0364a, 0449, 0450, 0455b, 0365-0371, 0007): all 68 numbers of the three bare passages agree with the transcription (the last number of p.573 looks like 369); about 60 of the 69 p.608 pairs, 35 p.600 pairs and 40 p.599 pairs were compared and agree. The p.608 truth file leaves out at least 13 groups that stand on the page (313 in 'connoisse', 32 290 85 60, 204 before 'envie', 261 310 133, 88 74 61 230 248 164), so T3 scores the pairs the transcriber aligned, not the whole page. On p.599 the number 30 stands over 're' in 'encore', so 'g' for 30 in B573 and B492 is against the key and is counted as a hole. The index entry (p.3), the signatures 'Baudouin' of 23 February and 7 March 1779, the sentence about the 'petit chiffre' and the cover to 'Van Temmel' were seen on the images. Founders Online returned an empty response to scripted requests, so the Franklin Papers notes were not checked here. Strict word shares: B573 13 of 18, B491 10 of 16, B492 1 of 4.

Follow-up to the review of PR #587: transcribed every code group of Baudouin's glossed letters pp.516-548 (pp.516, 526-531, 534-535, 547-548; 386 rows) with de Neufville's gloss over each, two passes on doubtful glosses (transcriptions/glossed_pp516-548.tsv). The other pages in the range carry no code. Corrections to the earlier gloss pairs: 474 (not 574) is 'déclaré' on p.516; 271 is 'le', not 'la', on p.526. New pairs include 400 = oi (three clear glosses), 143 = vaisseau(x) (p.534, faint, read the same in both passes), 98 = en, 237 = y, 39 = le Roi d'Espagne, 136 = au four more times.

Completed the p.608 truth file on the image (key/p608_truth_complete.tsv): 92 groups, 23 more than the 69 of heldout_p608_truth.tsv (313, 60, 11 38 141, 138 355 537, 455, 32 290 85 60, 204, 261 310 133, 88 74 61 230 248 164). Re-score of the frozen K2 on the whole page: 81 of 83 covered groups (the T3 pairs alone: 64 of 65); the new miss is 204 = 'le' for "l'" in "l'envie".

Round 4 test, plan written before the run (TEST_PLAN.md): every glossed group of the letter of 10 April 1779 (pp.529-531) held out; key K4 (205 numbers, sha256 3fa3b8ba...) frozen from all other sources; 64 of 66 covered held-out groups match the gloss (97%); 200 shuffled keys mean 0.6, max 6. The two misses are word forms (474 déclaré/déclarer, 384 passe/passez); 3 groups not covered (3, 6, 100).

Full key K5 (208 numbers, key/key_full_r4.json, sha256 146207b0...) frozen, then every open number of the bare passages retried. New: 143 = vaisseau in B492 ('d'acheter son vaisseau'); 136 settled as 'au' (5 votes to 1). Unchanged: 3 (taken at the time as glossed only as the numeral 3, p.529, which does not parse in B573; on 15 Nov 2026 that gloss was found to stand over the figure 6, so 3 has no gloss at all), 58, 227, 369/349, 30 (= re in de Neufville's draft; no gloss of 30 in Baudouin's letters), 162, 507, 501 (unglossed on p.529 too), and the B527 lines.

Founders Online in Chrome: Papers of Benjamin Franklin 28:353-354 nn.8-9 (Dumas to Franklin, 5 Jan 1779) names 'Sartine's associate Chaumont and secretary Baudouin' and cites the 23 Feb 1779 letter of this file; PBF 25:366-367 n.9 calls Baudouin 'Sartine's agent'. A search for 'Dunoyer' finds nothing on this correspondence. So Baudouin as Sartine's secretary is checked in print; 'Dunoyer' = Baudouin rests on the file itself (index, hand, signatures) and is not confirmed outside it.

Re-read the heading of p.498 on the image: 'A Paris le Lundy 7. mars 1779' (the 7 has the form of the 7s in '1779'; 'mars' is clear). 7 March 1779 was a Sunday; Monday was the 8th. The same writer's 'aujourd'huy mardy' on 30 March 1779 (p.516) is right for that date. Recorded as written; not emended.

Second pass: surveyed Baudouin's letters pp.487-515 and 549-590 page by page (transcriptions/survey_pp487-515_549-590.tsv): code only on the bare pp.491-492 and 573 and on p.579, whose two glossed groups (8 numbers) were transcribed in full (transcriptions/glossed_p579.tsv). Read by an AI agent on the images; no person has checked it.

T5: the frozen key_full_r4 (sha256 checked) scored on the five p.579 glossed groups never used to build it: 4 of 5 (miss 226, glossed 'Hollande' here and 'même' on p.606); 200 shuffled keys mean 0.04, at most 1. Correction of 15 Nov 2026: two of the five (68, 428) were already in the key through key_additions_round2.tsv (round 2), so the held-out set was wrong; of the three pairs new to the key (499, 202, 226) it predicts 2 (shuffles mean 0.03, at most 1); three pairs are too few to carry weight. Rebuilt key key_full_r5 was identical to key_full_r4 on 14 Nov (it counted 68 and 428 twice; rebuilt on 15 Nov after the p.529 correction it differs only in 6 = 3 and no value for 3); retry of the bare passages settles no open number (B573 13/18, B491 10/16, B492 2/4).

Integration review for the write-up: escalation checklist and gaps reviewed (every open number retried on all glossed pages; the remaining routes are the Archives nationales Marine B4/B7 and Dutch archives, not online); the "Dunoyer is Baudouin" gap given its blocker (needs-physical-access) and mirrored into outcome.gaps; Transcription doubts listed in NOTES; a crop of p.573 cut from the National Archives Catalog frame for the page.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.037; polyphony 0.036; 29 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.077

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The writer's own plain drafts with numbers written over them, and the recipient's glosses, give the code; a key frozen from some drafts predicts the others.

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: free images located, the code reconstructed from de Neufville's drafts and tested on held-out drafts, the leaf evidence for the index's identification of 'Dunoyer' as Baudouin, and the bare passages of pp.491-492 and 573 read. Checked by a second AI agent of ours, not by a person.
Jean de Neufville, who wrote the code numbers over his own drafts (who composed the code is not shown), and glossed some of Baudouin's letters; Baudouin, who read de Neufville's letters in it.
The Department of State clerk who indexed the volume (p.3): 'Du Noyer, Bowdoin or Mad. D. Arras'.

texts.label: B573, Dunoyer (Baudouin) to de Neufville, 24 January 1780
texts.summary: The patriarch and the merry band will make [them] swallow the last pill, to the shame of the States General; [3] long ago took 'the loan business' away from the [?]rands and gave it up; a loan nobody will put money into can only harm the credit of [369/349]; speak to 'M. du Fresne' (Chaumont). That the loan is the American loan is inference.
texts.note: Strict count at integration (14 Nov 2026), in words carried by code numbers: 13 of 18 = 72%. Holes: [3], [58]rands, [227]er, ar{g}ent (30 is 're' in the key; 'g' is set by the word) and the last number (369 or 349). The contributor's figure, counted in numbers with a key value: 39 of 43 = 91%. Follow-up (14 Nov 2026): no change after the retry with key_full_r4 (13 of 18); 136 is now 'au' in the key by 5 votes to 1.

reading_review.by: B. Dudout (review assisted by Claude, claude-opus-5-5)
reading_review.note: Read as French against the English: coherent; the four holes ([3], [58], [227], [369/349]) are marked and {g} is flagged. Compared with the image M332 roll 4 frame 0428 (p. 573, fol. 178): the clear text ('Je reçois monsieur l'honneur de la vôtre du 17 ... d'opprobre et de ridicule', 'Il y a longtemps que ... l'affaire de ...') and the groups 3 69 229 149 310 158 / 58 36 85 188 133 and 141 53 369 agree with the reading and decode. B: four of eighteen coded words are open.

texts.label: B491, Dunoyer (Baudouin) to de Neufville, 18 January 1780
texts.summary: On the Stadholder and the 'merry band'; V. Vort parades his intimacy with Leerding and boasts at court of successes he owes to the Pensionary of Amsterdam.
texts.note: Strict count at integration (14 Nov 2026): 10 of 16 units = 62% (ten words read; 507, 501, 405, 387, 390 and 447 unread). The contributor's figures: 12 of 18 numbers = 67%, or 12 of 14 if 405, 387, 390 and 447 are nulls, which is not shown. Follow-up (14 Nov 2026): no change after the retry with key_full_r4 (10 of 16).

reading_review.by: B. Dudout (review assisted by Claude, claude-opus-5-5)
reading_review.note: Read as French against the English: the three paragraphs are coherent; the coded words mostly name people (Stadhouder, Pensionnaire des Amsterdammois); [507] [501] are open and four groups are taken as nulls (NOTES). Image not re-checked by this reviewer for this letter. B.

texts.label: B492, same letter, second page
texts.summary: Offers to buy 'my aunt's' ship ('son vaisseau', 143) wait on 'the holy man'; jobbery over this [162] between V. Vort and [G]rand.
texts.note: Strict count, follow-up of 14 Nov 2026: 2 of 4 words = 50% ('vaisseau', from the gloss of 143 on p.534, and 'ce'; [162] is a hole and '{G}rand' is set by the word, 30 being 're' in the key). At integration: 1 of 4. The contributor's first figure: 5 of 7 numbers = 71%.

reading_review.by: B. Dudout (review assisted by Claude, claude-opus-5-5)
reading_review.note: Read as French against the English: two coherent sentences, carried by the clear text; of the four coded words, 143 = vaisseau (gloss p. 534) and {G}rand (30 = g by sense, against the draft's 're') are flagged and [162] stays open. Image not re-checked by this reviewer for this letter. B.

texts.label: B527, two unglossed lines of Dunoyer's letter of 9 April 1779
texts.summary: Decoded to syllables (one names Vergennes); not read.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Strict count, follow-up of 14 Nov 2026, in words carried by code numbers, sure words only: B573 13 of 18, B491 10 of 16, B492 2 of 4, together 25 of 38 = 66% (at integration 24 of 38 = 63%). A unit set by the word against the key ({g}), an open number and an unread number each count as a hole. The contributor's first figure, in numbers with a key value: 56 of 68 = 83%. B527 (15 numbers) decoded, not read. The drafts and glossed letters were read by their writer and recipient and are not counted.

gaps.detail: Retried with the full transcription of the glossed letters pp.516-548 (key_full_r4) and again after the survey of pp.487-515 and 549-590 and the p.579 glosses (key_full_r5, identical): none of these numbers is glossed with a value that fits; 3 has no gloss (the 'numeral 3' of p.529 stands over the figure 6; corrected 15 Nov 2026), 501 and 507 occur only unglossed or struck. Candidates in NOTES.md.

gaps.item: A glossed or deciphered copy of the bare groups (pp.491-492, 573)
gaps.detail: None in this file: all 808 images paged; pp.487-515 and 549-590 surveyed page by page (14 Nov 2026), the neighbours of the bare pages read, p.579 transcribed in full. Baudouin's office copies or de Neufville's sent letters may survive in the Archives nationales, Marine B4/B7, not seen.

gaps.item: That "Dunoyer" is Baudouin is not confirmed outside the file
gaps.detail: Rests on the volume's index, the signatures "Baudouin" on pp.497 and 499, the announced change of name and the same hand; a comparison with Baudouin's signed notes (American Philosophical Society) or his office papers (Archives nationales, Marine B4, B7) is needed.

outcome.notes: Most coded text in the file was read at the time: de Neufville's drafts carry his plain French, and he glossed many of Baudouin's letters. The volume's own 19th-century index identifies Du Noyer as Baudouin. What is new is the reconstruction of the code from the drafts, the leaf evidence for that identification, and the reading of the bare passages. PBF 28:354 n.9 cites one Baudouin letter of the file.
